1	# Epic 1 Context: Foundation & Session Management
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	This epic delivers the scaffold every other feature depends on: the pinned-stack project setup with its core infrastructure verified working together, the full visual design-token system, email/password authentication with silent session refresh, the session-expiry recovery overlay, and a base navigation shell with placeholders for everything not yet built. It is delivered first because every later epic assumes this foundation — DI, networking, error handling, session state, design tokens, and navigation — already exists and is stable. Users come away able to create an account, log in, stay logged in across restarts, recover gracefully if their session expires mid-use, and navigate the whole app shell even though most feature screens are still placeholders.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure
12	- Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library
13	- Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login
14	- Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence
15	- Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay
16	- Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders
17	
18	## Requirements & Constraints
19	
20	- Account creation and login round-trip through the backend with exactly two fields (email, password) — no password confirmation, no display-name field at signup. Login/signup/refresh are the only calls using the anon key; every other call uses the user's access token.
21	- A valid, unexpired session must persist across app restarts with no re-prompt; nearing/past-expiry sessions refresh silently with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds 300ms.
22	- When the backend reports an expired session, an overlay appears over whatever screen is active (never a navigation away); the underlying screen's state/scroll position is preserved; "Entrar novamente" leads to biometric/PIN re-auth, not a login form.
23	- All four base destinations (Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, Configurações) must be reachable from launch; any destination whose feature isn't built yet shows a visually distinct, fully-polished placeholder — never a broken link and never a visibly "unfinished" look.
24	- Local UI interactions must respond in <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator (manual timing spot-check, no automated perf tooling).
25	- Zero Clean Architecture layer violations: domain imports neither Flutter nor anything from a data layer.
26	- ≥80% domain-layer test coverage; the write-failure matrix (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types: timeout, malformed response, no connection = 15 scenarios) must be fully handled with zero unhandled exceptions — this epic builds the one shared, reusable test helper every later feature's write-endpoint tests reuse.
27	- Zero hardcoded visual values outside the design-tokens file; every control must honor Dynamic Type without truncating.
28	- An integration spike, before any other building, must prove `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one bootstrap — this combination is otherwise unverified.
29	
30	## Technical Decisions
31	
32	- Single DI container: exactly one `get_it` instance registered at bootstrap; `dio` is configured through it; secrets (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) load via `flutter_dotenv` from a gitignored `.env`, never hardcoded.
33	- One sealed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from the backend's error taxonomy plus a local-only `MalformedResponse`), defined once and never redefined/subset per feature; every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or a `Stream` for SSE), with no native/dio exception ever escaping unmapped.
34	- One retry interceptor on the `dio`/`ApiClient` layer retries only the 6 server-marked `retryable:true` codes; every other failure surfaces once, unretried.
35	- One URL builder maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` (never the literal OpenAPI REST path); one interceptor owns headers — `apikey` on every call, anon-key bearer token only on signup/login/refresh, user access token on everything else.
36	- Exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from the auth feature's domain layer and registered once in DI as a singleton; every later consumer (including RF07/Epic 4) injects/listens to it rather than re-deriving session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
37	- This epic builds the `go_router` redirect skeleton composing session state; Epic 2 (RF03) later plugs a local vault-status gate into the same redirect, checked before session status — this epic should leave that composition point open rather than hardcoding a session-only redirect.
38	- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
39	- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
40	- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
41	- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
46	- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
47	- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
48	- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
49	- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
50	- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
51	- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
56	- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
57	- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
58	- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
59	- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
60	- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).

---
failed_layers: '' # set at runtime: comma-separated list of layers that failed or returned empty
---

# Step 2: Review

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`
- All review subagents must run at the same model capability as the current session.
- Run subagents synchronously: launch them together, then wait for all results before continuing.

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. The review layers are `{workflow.review_layers}`, resolved during activation.

2. For each layer in `{workflow.review_layers}`:
   - `instruction` empty or missing → drop the layer silently (an override disabled it).
   - `when` condition present and not satisfied by the current context (`{review_mode}`, `{spec_file}`) → drop the layer and tell the user, e.g. "Acceptance Auditor skipped — no spec file provided."
   - otherwise → the layer is active.

   If no layer is active, HALT with status `blocked` and blocking condition `no active review layers`.

3. Execute all active layers in parallel wherever their execution methods allow: expand `{skill-root}` in each layer's `instruction` to this skill's absolute installed directory, then substitute the runtime placeholders (`{diff_output}`, `{spec_file}`). For an instruction that launches a reviewer subagent, launch that child with the prompt text after placeholder substitution; do not load the reviewer instruction file yourself. For any other customized instruction, execute it as written. Do not leave `{skill-root}` unresolved in a child prompt. If a layer's instruction requires subagents and subagents are not available, for each such layer write under `{implementation_artifacts}` the exact child prompt from that layer's instruction after placeholder substitution (not a path-only pointer), then HALT. Ask the user to run each in a separate session (ideally a different LLM) and paste back the findings. When findings are pasted, treat them as those layers' findings and resume from this point. This is the only allowed parent-side read of a reviewer instruction file.

4. **Layer failure handling**: If any layer fails, times out, or returns empty results, append the layer's `name` to `{failed_layers}` (comma-separated) and proceed with findings from the remaining layers.

5. Collect all findings from the completed layers, keeping track of each finding's originating layer `id`.

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-03-triage.md`

724	@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
725	+import 'dart:async';
726	+
727	+/// Story 1.5 — lets `core/network`'s `ApiClient` signal a mid-session
728	+/// `AUTH_EXPIRED` without importing anything from `features/auth` (RNF06:
729	+/// the domain/data layers of a feature are the only things allowed to know
730	+/// about each other across that boundary, never the other way from core).
731	+/// `SessionRepositoryImpl` is the one bridge that turns an event on
732	+/// [expiredEvents] into the epic's single `SessionStatus.expired` value on
733	+/// its own `statusStream` (Design Notes).
734	+///
735	+/// Pure Dart, no Flutter import — same constraint `ApiClient`/`Failure`
736	+/// already hold in `core/`.
737	+abstract class SessionExpiryNotifier {
738	+  /// Broadcast stream of expiry events. Unlike `SessionRepository
739	+  /// .statusStream`, this carries no replay semantics: it is a one-shot
740	+  /// signal per expiry, not a status a late subscriber needs to catch up
741	+  /// on — only `SessionRepositoryImpl`'s single long-lived subscription
742	+  /// (wired at construction) is expected to listen.
743	+  Stream<void> get expiredEvents;
744	+
745	+  /// Signals that the current session just expired mid-use (a non-boot
746	+  /// `AUTH_EXPIRED` response). Never throws.
747	+  void notifyExpired();
748	+
749	+  /// Releases the underlying stream resource.
750	+  Future<void> dispose();
751	+}
752	+
753	+/// Default implementation — a broadcast `StreamController` wrapped behind
754	+/// the port above.
755	+class SessionExpiryNotifierImpl implements SessionExpiryNotifier {
756	+  final StreamController<void> _controller = StreamController<void>.broadcast();
757	+
758	+  @override
759	+  Stream<void> get expiredEvents => _controller.stream;
760	+
761	+  @override
762	+  void notifyExpired() {
763	+    // Guards against a call racing `dispose()` (wired to `get_it`'s
764	+    // `sl.reset()`) — without this, a late `.add()` after `.close()` would
765	+    // throw an unhandled `StateError` instead of just being a no-op on an
766	+    // already-torn-down notifier (same rationale as `SessionRepositoryImpl
767	+    // ._emit`).
768	+    if (_controller.isClosed) {
769	+      return;
770	+    }
771	+    _controller.add(null);
772	+  }
773	+
774	+  @override
775	+  Future<void> dispose() => _controller.close();
776	+}

-  summary: `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s uncommitted fix (switched from a raw `AuthState(...)` constructor to `state.copyWith(...)` so an in-flight `status` survives a mode toggle) has no test that can actually observe the regression it fixes — every existing `toggleMode()` call site in the test suite toggles while `status` is already the default idle value.
-  evidence: Root cause is in `lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart`, pre-existing uncommitted work carried over from story 1.3's review loop, not touched by story 1.4's diff — surfaced incidentally by story 1.4's review because the dirty working tree put it in the reviewed diff. Needs a test that calls `submit()` to put `status` in a non-idle state, then `toggleMode()`, then asserts `status` is unchanged.
+  summary: `AuthCubit.toggleMode()`'s `state.copyWith(...)` fix (so an in-flight `status` survives a mode toggle, instead of the previous raw `AuthState(...)` constructor silently resetting it) has no test that can actually observe the regression it fixes — every existing `toggleMode()` call site in the test suite toggles while `status` is already the default idle value.
+  evidence: Code review of story-1-4 corrected this entry's earlier "not touched by story 1.4's diff" claim — the change to `lib/features/auth/presentation/cubit/auth_cubit.dart` IS part of this diff. It's deferred on its own merits instead: `toggleMode()`'s only call site is a button disabled whenever `isSubmitting` is true, and every submit-failure path resets `status` back to idle in the same `emit` that sets `formError` — so there is no path through the real `AuthScreen` that can currently drive `status` non-idle at the moment `toggleMode()` runs. Needs a test that calls `submit()` to put `status` in a non-idle state, then `toggleMode()`, then asserts `status` is unchanged — revisit if a future change makes that sequence reachable.

Needs a test that first drives `emailError` non-null (e.g. a failed local-validation submit with a malformed e-mail), then calls `passwordChanged`, then asserts `emailError` is now null.
+## Deferred from: code review of story-1-5-expired-session-recovery-overlay (2026-11-02)
+
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-5-expired-session-recovery-overlay.md`
+  summary: Nothing transitions `SessionStatus` back from `expired` to `authenticated` anywhere (`SessionRepositoryImpl`, `main.dart`), so once a user confirms "Entrar novamente" the status stream itself never leaves `expired` — only the UI route changes.
+  evidence: By design for this story: the frozen spec scopes "Entrar novamente" to a throwaway placeholder standing in for Epic 2's real biometric/PIN flow, and that epic is the one that will actually re-authenticate the user and needs to decide how/when the status returns to `authenticated`. Not a bug in this story's own scope (nothing today re-enters the `authenticated` screen while still showing stale `expired` state), but unlike this diff's own similarly-scoped `toggleMode` gap above, it wasn't recorded as a known future obligation — flagging here so Epic 2's own story doesn't have to rediscover it from scratch.

@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+import 'dart:async';
+
+/// Story 1.5 — lets `core/network`'s `ApiClient` signal a mid-session
+/// `AUTH_EXPIRED` without importing anything from `features/auth` (RNF06:
+/// the domain/data layers of a feature are the only things allowed to know
+/// about each other across that boundary, never the other way from core).
+/// `SessionRepositoryImpl` is the one bridge that turns an event on
+/// [expiredEvents] into the epic's single `SessionStatus.expired` value on
+/// its own `statusStream` (Design Notes).
+///
+/// Pure Dart, no Flutter import — same constraint `ApiClient`/`Failure`
+/// already hold in `core/`.
+abstract class SessionExpiryNotifier {
+  /// Broadcast stream of expiry events. Unlike `SessionRepository
+  /// .statusStream`, this carries no replay semantics: it is a one-shot
+  /// signal per expiry, not a status a late subscriber needs to catch up
+  /// on — only `SessionRepositoryImpl`'s single long-lived subscription
+  /// (wired at construction) is expected to listen.
+  Stream<void> get expiredEvents;
+
+  /// Signals that the current session just expired mid-use (a non-boot
+  /// `AUTH_EXPIRED` response). Never throws.
+  void notifyExpired();
+
+  /// Releases the underlying stream resource.
+  Future<void> dispose();
+}
+
+/// Default implementation — a broadcast `StreamController` wrapped behind
+/// the port above.
+class SessionExpiryNotifierImpl implements SessionExpiryNotifier {
+  final StreamController<void> _controller = StreamController<void>.broadcast();
+
+  @override
+  Stream<void> get expiredEvents => _controller.stream;
+
+  @override
+  void notifyExpired() {
+    // Guards against a call racing `dispose()` (wired to `get_it`'s
+    // `sl.reset()`) — without this, a late `.add()` after `.close()` would
+    // throw an unhandled `StateError` instead of just being a no-op on an
+    // already-torn-down notifier (same rationale as `SessionRepositoryImpl
+    // ._emit`).
+    if (_controller.isClosed) {
+      return;
+    }
+    _controller.add(null);
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Future<void> dispose() => _controller.close();
+}

+/// `scrimIn` (0.18s ease-out fade) as the only entrance choreography, and
+/// at most one instance open at a time — [show] is the one way this

+/// no caller has to re-implement it.

+  const ConfirmationDialog({

+    required this.title,
+    required this.message,
+    required this.confirmLabel,

+  final String message;
+  final String confirmLabel;

+  /// or destructive (`colorError`, a later story's account-deletion
+  /// confirm) — never any other color (Boundaries: "neutral
+  /// `colorTextPrimary` title, never `colorError`" for *this* story's own
+  /// call site).
+  final Color titleColor;

+  /// posição do scroll são preservados"). Optional — a future destructive
+  /// confirmation has no equivalent.
+  final String? caption;

+  /// for tests; callers should not need to read it directly.

+        // before (the min-height constraint is satisfied with room to
+        // spare, so `Center` centers within it), but under an extreme
+        // Dynamic Type scale — where the card's intrinsic height can
+        // exceed the screen — this scrolls instead of overflowing
+        // (RNF08's "no control truncates under Dynamic Type").

+            child: ConstrainedBox(

+  @override

+    return Container(
+      padding: DesignTokens.dialogCardPadding,
+      decoration: const BoxDecoration(
+        color: DesignTokens.colorSurfaceElevated,
+        borderRadius: BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(DesignTokens.radiusLg)),
+        boxShadow: DesignTokens.elevation2,
+      ),
+      child: Column(
+        mainAxisSize: MainAxisSize.min,
+        crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.stretch,
+        children: [

+                icon,
+                size: DesignTokens.dialogIconSize,
+                color: DesignTokens.colorPrimary,
+              ),
+              const SizedBox(width: DesignTokens.spacingSm),
+              Expanded(
+                child: Text(
+                  title,
+                  style: DesignTokens.textTitleSm.copyWith(color: titleColor),
+                ),
+              ),
+            ],
+          ),
+          const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.dialogContentGap),
+          Text(
+            message,
+            style: DesignTokens.textBodyMd.copyWith(
+              color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
+            ),
+          ),
+          const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.dialogContentGap),
+          AppButton(label: confirmLabel, onPressed: onConfirm),
+          if (caption != null) ...[
+            const SizedBox(height: DesignTokens.dialogContentGap),
+            Text(
+              caption!,
+              textAlign: TextAlign.center,
+              style: DesignTokens.textMonoCaption.copyWith(
+                color: DesignTokens.colorTextSecondary,
+              ),
+            ),
+          ],
+        ],
+      ),

+}

  Result: no violations found. This diff tracks the frozen spec closely and correctly. Specifics checked and confirmed clean:
  
  - Detection point (lib/core/network/api_client.dart:107-147): notifies SessionExpiryNotifier only when `failure is AuthExpired && !_isAnonKeyOnlyCall(e)`, where `_isAnonKeyOnlyCall` mirrors `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf`/`anonKeyOnlyFunctions` (confirmed those are public statics in header_interceptor.dart:20-24,80-83) with the same fail-open try/catch. `auth-refresh` is in that set, so boot-time refresh never fires the notifier — verified by both api_client_test.dart and the real-wiring network_pipeline_integration_test.dart.
  - SessionStatus (session_status.dart): exactly one value added (`expired`); doc-comment grammar fix from the Review Findings is present.
  - Bridge (session_repository_impl.dart:28-109): `_onSessionExpired()` emits `expired` only when `_lastStatus == authenticated`; `_lastStatus` defaults to null, so a pre-boot event, a post-logout event, and a second event while already `expired` are all correctly silent no-ops (matches the I/O matrix and has direct test coverage for each row). `dispose()` cancels `_expirySubscription` before closing `_statusController`, both isClosed-guarded.
  - RNF06: SessionExpiryNotifier (core/session/session_expiry_notifier.dart) imports only dart:async; no Flutter/feature import anywhere in core/.
  - Overlay widget (confirmation_dialog.dart): `barrierDismissible: false` + `PopScope(canPop: false)` block both scrim-tap and back-gesture; `isOpen` guard is try/catch-safe; default `titleColor` is `colorTextPrimary` (never `colorError`) at this story's one call site in main.dart, while the widget itself stays reusable for Epic 8 exactly as the Design Notes prescribe.
  - Visual tokens: `colorScrim = Color(0x38241F19)` — decoded the raw prototype HTML directly and confirmed `rgba(36,31,25,.22)` → exactly `0x38241F19`. `dialogIconSize=20`, `dialogContentGap=14`, `dialogScreenMargin=20px`, `dialogCardPadding=24/20`, and `radiusLg=24`/`elevation2` (`0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)`) all match the prototype's inline styles for this specific overlay block exactly.
  - Copy: title/message/caption/button-label in main.dart are byte-for-byte the same strings as the raw prototype's `sessionExpiredVisible` block ("Sua sessão expirou por segurança...", "o histórico e a posição do scroll são preservados"), satisfying the "never implies data loss, states history/scroll preserved" boundary.
  - Screen-instance preservation: both `authenticated` and `expired` render `const _PostAuthPlaceholder()` from the same StreamBuilder branch, so Flutter's element reconciliation keeps the same Element/State — matches "widget instance never replaced," and is asserted in main_test.dart.
  - One-shot overlay guard: `_expiryOverlayShown` in `_CerneAppState` correctly distinguishes "already confirmed, don't reopen on rebuild" from `ConfirmationDialog.isOpen`'s "currently stacked" guard — both are necessary and both are tested.
  - DI wiring (injection_container.dart, auth_injection.dart): SessionExpiryNotifier registered as a singleton with `dispose:` before ApiClient, and threaded into both ApiClient and SessionRepositoryImpl via the same instance — no second notifier, no second stream.
  - Never-list: no go_router, no Epic 2 biometric/PIN logic (just a one-line `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` stub), no new icon-font dependency (`Icons.lock_outline` approximates `ph-lock-key`), no Reduce-Motion code.
  - All 10 pre-baked Review Findings in the spec file (grammar fix, reopen-guard, PopScope, exception-safe show(), onError on the subscription, empty-refresh-token test, dispose-regression test, focus-trap test, scrim-absorption test) are all present and implemented exactly as described.
  
  I did not find any genuine AC violation, spec-intent deviation, missing behavior, or spec/code contradiction. The unrelated formatting-only changes elsewhere in the diff (app_button.dart, app_text_field.dart, avatar.dart, component_library_interaction_test.dart, doc/spec-file updates for stories 1.2–1.4) are out of this story's scope and contain no functional changes that bear on Story 1.5's AC.

[Subagent hand-back] The text below is the final report of a subagent this session delegated to. Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows:
  ### Untested guard-release path when `ConfirmationDialog.show()` throws synchronously
  
  - **Changed surface:** `lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart:74-108` — `ConfirmationDialog.show()` sets the static single-overlay guard `isOpen = true` (line 74), then wraps the `showGeneralDialog` call in `try { ... } catch (_) { isOpen = false; rethrow; }` (lines 75-108) so that a *synchronous* throw from `showGeneralDialog` (the code's own comment: "e.g. a future caller passing a `context` with no `Navigator` ancestor") still releases the guard, instead of leaving `isOpen` stuck at `true` forever. This `try`/`catch` is new code added by this story specifically to fix that failure mode (the test-summary and spec docs list it as one of four gaps "surfaced and fixed before landing").
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** `lib/main.dart:121` (`_maybeShowExpiryOverlay`'s call to `ConfirmationDialog.show(...)`) is the only current call site, but the guard is a `static` field shared by *every* future call too (the widget's own doc comment says Epic 8's account-deletion confirm will reuse the same `show()`/`isOpen` guard).
  - **Existing test evidence:** I read the entirety of `test/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog_test.dart` (313 lines) and `test/main_test.dart`'s new "Story 1.5" group. Every test there calls `ConfirmationDialog.show()` with a `context` that does have a `Navigator` ancestor (`MaterialApp` → `Builder`/`Scaffold`), so `showGeneralDialog` never throws synchronously in any of them — the `catch` branch is never executed by any test. I also grepped the whole repo for `ConfirmationDialog` (`grep -rn "ConfirmationDialog" test/ lib/`) and found no test that constructs a context without a `Navigator` ancestor or otherwise forces `showGeneralDialog` to throw. `setUp(() => ConfirmationDialog.isOpen = false)` in both test files only resets the flag between tests; it doesn't exercise the exception path.
  - **Missing verification:** no assertion that (a) `isOpen` becomes `false` again after a failed `show()` call, or equivalently (b) a subsequent, valid `show()` call still succeeds after one `show()` call failed synchronously.
  - **Demonstration:** delete the `try { ... } catch (_) { isOpen = false; rethrow; }` wrapper (i.e. revert to directly `return showGeneralDialog(...).whenComplete(() => isOpen = false);`, with no catch). If any future call to `show()` throws before `showGeneralDialog` returns a `Future` (the exact scenario the comment names), `isOpen` is left permanently `true`, and `.whenComplete()` never attaches/runs because the exception happened before the chained call. Every later `ConfirmationDialog.show()` call across the entire app — not just the failing one — would silently no-op forever (the `if (isOpen) return Future<void>.value();` early return at line 71-73), so the session-expiry overlay (and any future reuse, e.g. Epic 8's deletion-confirm dialog) would stop appearing for the rest of the app's lifetime. None of the tests I checked would fail: they never put `show()` into the throwing branch, so they can't observe whether the `catch` block's `isOpen = false` ever ran.
  - **Consequence:** if this specific recovery branch regresses (reverted, or the `isOpen = false` inside `catch` is dropped while keeping `rethrow`), the whole suite stays green while a single bad `show()` call — now or after a future caller is added — would permanently disable the overlay guard for the rest of the running app.
  - **Suggested test shape:** a unit/widget test that calls `ConfirmationDialog.show()` with a `BuildContext` lacking a `Navigator` ancestor (e.g. `pumpWidget` a bare `Container`/`View` with no `MaterialApp`/`Navigator`, then call `show()` from a `Builder` inside it) to force the synchronous throw, assert the call throws, then assert `ConfirmationDialog.isOpen` is `false` afterward (or that an immediately-following valid `show()` call actually opens the dialog).
  
  No other verification gaps found in this diff. I traced the rest of the behavioral surface — `ApiClient`'s new `AUTH_EXPIRED`→`SessionExpiryNotifier.notifyExpired()` detection (incl. the anon-key-only exclusion), `SessionExpiryNotifierImpl`, `SessionRepositoryImpl`'s bridge from `expiredEvents` onto `SessionStatus.expired` (incl. the "only from `authenticated`", "no re-emit once already `expired`", and `dispose()`-cancels-subscription cases), the empty-refresh-token short-circuit in `restoreSession()`, `main.dart`'s `_statusStream` caching, `_expiryOverlayShown` one-shot guard, and the `PopScope`/non-dismissible-barrier/focus-trap behavior of `ConfirmationDialog` itself — and each of those is exercised by an assertion that would actually fail under the corresponding regression (`test/core/network/api_client_test.dart`, `test/core/network/network_pipeline_integration_test.dart`, `test/core/session/session_expiry_notifier_test.dart`, `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart`, `test/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog_test.dart`, `test/main_test.dart`'s "Story 1.5" group). The `_isAnonKeyOnlyCall` catch-block in `lib/core/network/api_client.dart:139-146` (mirroring `HeaderInterceptor.onRequest`'s own fail-open catch) is also untested, but I checked `HeaderInterceptor.functionNameOf` (`lib/core/network/header_interceptor.dart:80-83`, unmodified by this diff) and it only does `Uri.parse(path).pathSegments` — not realistically throwing for any path `UrlBuilder` produces — so I dropped it as not a demonstrable regression, consistent with how this project's own deferred-work.md already treats similarly unreachable guard code.
  
  ## Other findings
  
  - None beyond the gap above — I did not notice any additional non-gap defects while tracing this diff's verification paths.
</agent-message>

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

60	  /// focus-trapped overlay above whatever screen is currently showing,
61	  /// without replacing it — the underlying route stays mounted, so its
62	  /// scroll/state is preserved (Boundaries: "the authenticated screen's
63	  /// widget instance is never replaced").
64	  ///
65	  /// A second call while one is already open is a silent no-op (I/O
66	  /// matrix: "already-open overlay ... no second dialog stacks").
67	  static Future<void> show({
68	    required BuildContext context,
69	    required WidgetBuilder builder,
70	  }) {
71	    if (isOpen) {
72	      return Future<void>.value();
73	    }
74	    isOpen = true;
75	    try {
76	      return showGeneralDialog<void>(
77	        context: context,
78	        barrierDismissible: false,
79	        // The framework's own `ModalBarrier` stays fully transparent — the
80	        // scrim actually seen on screen is this widget's own `build()`
81	        // below, which lets `transitionBuilder` fade the scrim and the card
82	        // together as one `scrimIn` choreography instead of two separately
83	        // animated layers.
84	        barrierColor: Colors.transparent,
85	        transitionDuration: const Duration(milliseconds: 180),
86	        transitionBuilder: (context, animation, secondaryAnimation, child) {
87	          return FadeTransition(
88	            opacity: CurvedAnimation(
89	              parent: animation,
90	              curve: Curves.easeOut,
91	            ),
92	            child: child,
93	          );
94	        },
95	        pageBuilder: (context, animation, secondaryAnimation) => PopScope(
96	          // UX-DR16/25/27/36 — non-dismissible: `barrierDismissible: false`
97	          // above only stops a scrim tap; without this, the system/hardware
98	          // back gesture would still pop the route and close the overlay.
99	          canPop: false,
100	          child: builder(context),
101	        ),
102	      ).whenComplete(() => isOpen = false);
103	    } catch (_) {
104	      // A synchronous throw from `showGeneralDialog` (e.g. a future caller
105	      // passing a `context` with no `Navigator` ancestor) must still release
106	      // the guard — otherwise every later `show()` call, from any caller,
107	      // silently no-ops forever.
108	      isOpen = false;
109	      rethrow;

Once there, `_expiryOverlayShown` is already `true` (one-shot guard) and `SessionRepositoryImpl._onSessionExpired()` only re-emits from `authenticated` (never from `expired`), so no later `AUTH_EXPIRED` response can ever reopen the overlay — the user is stuck looking "authenticated" with a dead session until they restart the app, with no visible error. A rapid double-tap can fire `onConfirm` twice — the second `Navigator.of(dialogContext).pop()` races the first pop already in flight, and the second `Navigator.of(context).push(...)` pushes a duplicate `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` onto the stack. - [ ] [Review][Patch] `ConfirmationDialog.show()`'s `catch (_) { isOpen = false; rethrow; }` branch — added specifically so a synchronous throw from `showGeneralDialog` (e.g. a future caller passing a `context` with no `Navigator` ancestor) doesn't permanently lock the app-wide single-overlay guard — has no test exercising it. Every test in `confirmation_dialog_test.dart` and `main_test.dart` calls `show()` with a context that does have a `Navigator` ancestor, so the branch never runs; a regression here (e.g. dropping the `catch`, or dropping `isOpen = false` inside it) would leave the whole suite green while silently disabling every future `ConfirmationDialog.show()` call — including Epic 8's account-deletion dialog, which reuses the same static guard — for the rest of the running app. Fix: add a test that forces the synchronous throw (e.g. call `show()` from a `Builder` with no `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` ancestor) and assert `isOpen` is `false` afterward. [lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart:67-111]

Fix: add the matching `dialogContext.mounted` check for consistency. [lib/main.dart:132-136]

101	### Code Review (2026-11-02)
102	
103	- [x] [Review][Defer] `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` (the "Entrar novamente" destination) has no `PopScope`/back-gesture guard, unlike `ConfirmationDialog`'s own route — the system back gesture pops straight back to `_PostAuthPlaceholder`, which still renders exactly like a normal authenticated screen even though `SessionStatus` is still `expired`. Once there, `_expiryOverlayShown` is already `true` (one-shot guard) and `SessionRepositoryImpl._onSessionExpired()` only re-emits from `authenticated` (never from `expired`), so no later `AUTH_EXPIRED` response can ever reopen the overlay — the user is stuck looking "authenticated" with a dead session until they restart the app, with no visible error. Deferred rather than patched now: the frozen spec explicitly scopes this screen as a throwaway placeholder Epic 2 deletes wholesale, and adding a back-gesture block today would just trade a silently-stuck-but-recoverable-by-restart state for a true dead end, without building the real fix (Epic 2's actual biometric/PIN flow is what will own a correct back-navigation story here). [lib/main.dart:217-229] — deferred, Epic 2's concern
104	- [ ] [Review][Patch] "Entrar novamente" has no debounce: `AppButton` has no built-in disable-after-tap (pre-existing, already deferred in story 1.2's own review), and the dialog's 180ms exit `FadeTransition` leaves the button hit-testable while fading out. A rapid double-tap can fire `onConfirm` twice — the second `Navigator.of(dialogContext).pop()` races the first pop already in flight, and the second `Navigator.of(context).push(...)` pushes a duplicate `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` onto the stack. Fix: guard `onConfirm` with a one-shot flag (same pattern already used for `_expiryOverlayShown`), or disable the button synchronously on first tap. [lib/main.dart:132-142]
105	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `ConfirmationDialog.show()`'s `catch (_) { isOpen = false; rethrow; }` branch — added specifically so a synchronous throw from `showGeneralDialog` (e.g. a future caller passing a `context` with no `Navigator` ancestor) doesn't permanently lock the app-wide single-overlay guard — has no test exercising it. Every test in `confirmation_dialog_test.dart` and `main_test.dart` calls `show()` with a context that does have a `Navigator` ancestor, so the branch never runs; a regression here (e.g. dropping the `catch`, or dropping `isOpen = false` inside it) would leave the whole suite green while silently disabling every future `ConfirmationDialog.show()` call — including Epic 8's account-deletion dialog, which reuses the same static guard — for the rest of the running app. Fix: add a test that forces the synchronous throw (e.g. call `show()` from a `Builder` with no `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` ancestor) and assert `isOpen` is `false` afterward. [lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart:67-111]
106	- [ ] [Review][Patch] The five new `DesignTokens` constants this story adds (`colorScrim`, `dialogIconSize`, `dialogContentGap`, `dialogScreenMargin`, `dialogCardPadding`) have no direct value assertion in `design_tokens_test.dart` — they're only ever passed through as parameters in `confirmation_dialog_test.dart`, never asserted against a rendered value. Breaks the per-token test convention story 1.2's own review established (e.g. its "layout insets" test group for `buttonPadding`/`textFieldContentPadding`). Fix: add assertions for the five new constants to `design_tokens_test.dart`. [test/core/design_tokens_test.dart]
107	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_maybeShowExpiryOverlay` calls `ConfirmationDialog.show(...)` as a bare, un-awaited statement inside a (non-`async`) `addPostFrameCallback` callback — inconsistent with this same file's own `unawaited(...)` convention a few lines above for exactly this situation. If the dialog's `Future` ever completes with an error, it becomes an unhandled `Future` rejection instead of a logged message. Fix: wrap the call in `unawaited(...)`. [lib/main.dart:121]
108	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `class MockSessionExpiryNotifier extends Mock implements SessionExpiryNotifier {}` is declared identically in both `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` and `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart` instead of one shared test helper. Fix: factor into a single shared mock (e.g. alongside the project's other shared test helpers). [test/core/network/api_client_test.dart, test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart]
109	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `api_client_test.dart`'s "a non-AUTH_EXPIRED failure never notifies, even on a bearer function" test throws a `DioException` built from the `setUp`-level `requestOptions` fixture (path `auth-signup`, anon-key-only) while the call under test actually targets `entries-create` (bearer) — currently harmless (the thrown `connectionError` type never reaches the anon-key-only check at all), but the fixture contradicts the scenario the test's own name describes. Fix: build a `RequestOptions` for `entries-create` for this test instead of reusing the shared anon-key fixture. [test/core/network/api_client_test.dart]
110	- [ ] [Review][Patch] `main.dart`'s `onConfirm` checks `context.mounted` before pushing the follow-up route but never checks `dialogContext.mounted` before the `Navigator.of(dialogContext).pop()` call immediately preceding it — an inconsistent mounted-guard pattern, though unreachable today (the callback only ever fires from a live tap on a still-mounted dialog). ### Code Review (2026-11-02)

- [x] [Review][Defer] `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` (the "Entrar novamente" destination) has no `PopScope`/back-gesture guard, unlike `ConfirmationDialog`'s own route — the system back gesture pops straight back to `_PostAuthPlaceholder`, which still renders exactly like a normal authenticated screen even though `SessionStatus` is still `expired`. Once there, `_expiryOverlayShown` is already `true` (one-shot guard) and `SessionRepositoryImpl._onSessionExpired()` only re-emits from `authenticated` (never from `expired`), so no later `AUTH_EXPIRED` response can ever reopen the overlay — the user is stuck looking "authenticated" with a dead session until they restart the app, with no visible error. Deferred rather than patched now: the frozen spec explicitly scopes this screen as a throwaway placeholder Epic 2 deletes wholesale, and adding a back-gesture block today would just trade a silently-stuck-but-recoverable-by-restart state for a true dead end, without building the real fix (Epic 2's actual biometric/PIN flow is what will own a correct back-navigation story here). [lib/main.dart:217-229] — deferred, Epic 2's concern
- [ ] [Review][Patch] "Entrar novamente" has no debounce: `AppButton` has no built-in disable-after-tap (pre-existing, already deferred in story 1.2's own review), and the dialog's 180ms exit `FadeTransition` leaves the button hit-testable while fading out. A rapid double-tap can fire `onConfirm` twice — the second `Navigator.of(dialogContext).pop()` races the first pop already in flight, and the second `Navigator.of(context).push(...)` pushes a duplicate `_BiometricReauthPlaceholder` onto the stack. Fix: guard `onConfirm` with a one-shot flag (same pattern already used for `_expiryOverlayShown`), or disable the button synchronously on first tap. [lib/main.dart:132-142]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `ConfirmationDialog.show()`'s `catch (_) { isOpen = false; rethrow; }` branch — added specifically so a synchronous throw from `showGeneralDialog` (e.g. a future caller passing a `context` with no `Navigator` ancestor) doesn't permanently lock the app-wide single-overlay guard — has no test exercising it. Every test in `confirmation_dialog_test.dart` and `main_test.dart` calls `show()` with a context that does have a `Navigator` ancestor, so the branch never runs; a regression here (e.g. dropping the `catch`, or dropping `isOpen = false` inside it) would leave the whole suite green while silently disabling every future `ConfirmationDialog.show()` call — including Epic 8's account-deletion dialog, which reuses the same static guard — for the rest of the running app. Fix: add a test that forces the synchronous throw (e.g. call `show()` from a `Builder` with no `MaterialApp`/`Navigator` ancestor) and assert `isOpen` is `false` afterward. [lib/core/widgets/confirmation_dialog.dart:67-111]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] The five new `DesignTokens` constants this story adds (`colorScrim`, `dialogIconSize`, `dialogContentGap`, `dialogScreenMargin`, `dialogCardPadding`) have no direct value assertion in `design_tokens_test.dart` — they're only ever passed through as parameters in `confirmation_dialog_test.dart`, never asserted against a rendered value. Breaks the per-token test convention story 1.2's own review established (e.g. its "layout insets" test group for `buttonPadding`/`textFieldContentPadding`). Fix: add assertions for the five new constants to `design_tokens_test.dart`. [test/core/design_tokens_test.dart]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `_maybeShowExpiryOverlay` calls `ConfirmationDialog.show(...)` as a bare, un-awaited statement inside a (non-`async`) `addPostFrameCallback` callback — inconsistent with this same file's own `unawaited(...)` convention a few lines above for exactly this situation. If the dialog's `Future` ever completes with an error, it becomes an unhandled `Future` rejection instead of a logged message. Fix: wrap the call in `unawaited(...)`. [lib/main.dart:121]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `class MockSessionExpiryNotifier extends Mock implements SessionExpiryNotifier {}` is declared identically in both `test/core/network/api_client_test.dart` and `test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart` instead of one shared test helper. Fix: factor into a single shared mock (e.g. alongside the project's other shared test helpers). [test/core/network/api_client_test.dart, test/features/auth/data/repositories/session_repository_impl_test.dart]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `api_client_test.dart`'s "a non-AUTH_EXPIRED failure never notifies, even on a bearer function" test throws a `DioException` built from the `setUp`-level `requestOptions` fixture (path `auth-signup`, anon-key-only) while the call under test actually targets `entries-create` (bearer) — currently harmless (the thrown `connectionError` type never reaches the anon-key-only check at all), but the fixture contradicts the scenario the test's own name describes. Fix: build a `RequestOptions` for `entries-create` for this test instead of reusing the shared anon-key fixture. [test/core/network/api_client_test.dart]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `main.dart`'s `onConfirm` checks `context.mounted` before pushing the follow-up route but never checks `dialogContext.mounted` before the `Navigator.of(dialogContext).pop()` call immediately preceding it — an inconsistent mounted-guard pattern, though unreachable today (the callback only ever fires from a live tap on a still-mounted dialog). Fix: add the matching `dialogContext.mounted` check for consistency. [lib/main.dart:132-136]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `injection_container.dart`'s comment says `SessionExpiryNotifier` is "registered before `ApiClient` so it's ready to inject" — but `registerLazySingleton` resolves its factory lazily on first `sl<T>()` access, not at registration time, so registration order isn't actually why the wiring works. Fix: reword the comment to not claim a causal ordering effect that `get_it`'s lazy singletons don't have. [lib/core/di/injection_container.dart:40-43]
- [x] [Review][Defer] `_expiryOverlayShown` is set to `true` *before* confirming `ConfirmationDialog.show()` actually presented anything. If `show()` silently no-ops because `ConfirmationDialog.isOpen` is already held by a different consumer (e.g. a future Epic 8 account-deletion dialog open at the same moment), the session-expiry overlay never appears and this flag is never reset — the user is stuck in `expired` with no visible recovery until the other dialog closes and nothing re-triggers this one. Unreachable today: `ConfirmationDialog` has exactly one call site in the whole app. Revisit when a second consumer (Epic 8) is added.
